thesis_text:
Bottom line: for Ramp (Software Engineering (SWE), entry), your odds through the cold application alone are low, but not zero. This read rests on a curated-qualitative record as of 2026-10-12 with no population sample — treat every pattern below as reported, not measured. Builder bar: Ramp's official page says it only hires builders and frames its founding hiring test in founder-like terms; candidate reports describe practical system-building assessments. No pass rate is published in fetched sources.

Who gets in (sample N=not available — curated-qualitative record, as of 2026-10-12):
- This CIR is curated-qualitative: no population sample exists for it yet, so there are no percentages to show. What follows is the reported pattern from public sources, labeled as such.
Known biases of this data: Survivorship bias: candidate-report guides reflect people who interviewed, disproportionately those who progressed.; Secondary-source risk: intern posting dates/pay come from a guide summarizing Ashby postings, not from a fetched Ashby posting body (the Ashby page renders via JavaScript and returned no posting text when fetched).; Official careers page is deliberately provocative employer marketing; treat its culture claims as stated, not revealed, preference.; No H-1B LCA, university-outcome or licensed population data was fetched in this pass.. We see who got in, not who tried and failed — survivorship bias is real (§0).

What Ramp says it screens for vs what the record shows:
Stated: Official careers page signals extreme ownership, pace and responsibility beyond the job description as the norm, and explicitly warns the environment is not for most people. Candidate reports describe behavioral probing for real iteration and scope-cutting to ship, and rejection risk from treating practical rounds as puzzles.
Revealed: 

Routes in, ranked for you:
First: SWE intern application on Ramp's Ashby board during the fall posting window (entry-level cohort) — See route details.
Second: Direct application to an open experienced SWE role via the official careers page / Ashby — See route details.
Third: Referral submitted by the referrer through the job board — See route details.

Your gap analysis (highest-leverage fix first: experience):
- school: you — not on file | cohort — See the school pattern in this CIR — stated qualitatively unless the CIR is population-backed; school is not in the user's control, so the plan routes around it (§3.1). | gap | fix: Do not plan around changing schools; offset with experience, projects and referrals.
- experience: you — no internships yet | cohort — Builder bar: Ramp's official page says it only hires builders and frames its founding hiring test in founder-like terms; candidate reports describe practical system-building assessments. No pass rate is published in fetched sources. | gap | fix: Land one real internship or role at a smaller, reachable employer first — the ladder pattern in this CIR's path patterns.
- projects: you — no projects on file | cohort — Revealed screen in this CIR: evidence of building or analyzing real things (see screening_signals.revealed). | gap | fix: Ship one project that solves a messy real problem for a real user, and document it.
- skills: you — no skills on file | cohort — not on file | unknown
- timing: you — year not on file | cohort — Dates are cycle-specific and date-stamped 2026-10-12; re-verify next cycle (Doc 3 §3.3). | unknown
- authorization: you — not on file | cohort — Sponsorship history is a matter of public record (DOL H-1B LCA filings); this CIR states only what its sources support, and immigration specifics go to the school's international office (§4.8 Q26 — not legal advice). | gap | fix: Confirm sponsorship for this exact role family before investing a season of prep; target employers with a filing history for the role.

Coffee-chat strategy: target the profile types named in the ranked routes — recent hires in this role family, alumni of your school now inside, and people one rung up the ladder you are climbing. Ask what the interviews actually test, what surprised them after starting, and what they would do with a semester to prepare. Keep asks short and specific; send the follow-up you promised.

Timeline and key dates: Dates are cycle-specific and date-stamped 2026-10-12; re-verify next cycle (Doc 3 §3.3). (as of 2026-10-12; recruiting dates shift every cycle — re-check the official careers page before acting, §3.3).

Risks and alternatives: Candidate-report compilation lists early over-abstraction in the progressive assessment, polished-but-empty behavioral stories, and missing quantitative estimates in system design as rejection patterns. Official careers page itself is a red-flag filter by design: it is written to persuade people who do not want extreme pace and responsibility not to apply. Adjacent options with similar signal: the other employers and role families whose CIRs share this ladder — the first rung matters more than the logo on it.

Want me to execute? I can build the coffee-chat target list from these routes, tailor your resume to this record's revealed screens (truthfully — only what you have actually done), and set the plan's reminders. Say the word and I start with the list.
